messages:
Maya (oncall): taking over handoff for night shift — ongoing kv-cache eviction spike in eu-central dedicated pool. active alert group: kv_eviction_rate_high, request_5xx_increase. I will be primary until 06:30 UTC. Carlos you good for secondary?
Carlos (secondary): yup I'm on secondary. will watch the pager and cover escalations.
incbot: ALERT (kv_eviction_rate_high) — 17 hosts in eu-central showing >30 evictions/minute. severity: P2. triggered at 2177777200
Maya (oncall): customer impact: a handful of mid-market customers on dedicated capacity seeing degraded encode latency and occasional 502s on RPCs that touch kv-store. not platform-wide. Lina from prod-eng pinged me earlier.
Lena (prod-eng): confirm we've got increased eviction churn after the 04:12 deploy to routing/scheduler v3.4.2. hypothesis: prefetch policy + new health-check scheduling causing hot shards to thrash.
Jin (sre): quick checklist I'm running: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-eu | grep kv` -> check OOMKilled/RestartCount; metrics: `sum(evictions_total) by (instance)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(kv_op_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))`. share links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv/evictions?orgId=1
Maya (oncall): current mitigations in progress: 1) rolling `routing/scheduler` v3.4.2 -> v3.4.1 on eu-controlled hosts (canary already done, 3/20 hosts rolled back). 2) temporarily bump eviction threshold for hot-shard policy on eu pool (see runbook snippet below). 3) enabled short-term rate-limit rule for prefetchers to lower burst.
Carlos (secondary): I applied the rate-limit rule at 2177777405 — new rule id rl-prefetch-eu-2177. observed ~18% drop in eviction rate on canary hosts.
Maya (oncall): good. I'll continue rollbacks one ring at a time. ETA for next ring 8 mins. please don't do config changes elsewhere.
deploy-bot: Deploy rollback initiated: routing/scheduler v3.4.2 -> v3.4.1 by Maya at 2177777480. progress 5/20 hosts.
Lena (prod-eng): note: plan B if rollback doesn't stabilize: disable prefetch on affected clusters and switch to read-through bypass for small windows. that'll increase RUC but reduce eviction churn.
Jin (sre): I pushed a short runbook snippet to the thread: ```Runbook: KV eviction surge — quick mitigation steps
1) Add RL: curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/ratelimit -d '{"id":"rl-prefetch","limit":2000,"window_ms":60000,"scope":"prefetch"}'
2) Bump eviction threshold: curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/kvpolicy -d '{"threshold":50}'
3) Rollback routing scheduler: /scripts/rollbacks/rollback_scheduler.sh eu 1
4) If still failing, disable prefetch: /scripts/prefetch toggle eu off
```
Maya (oncall): docs links: runbook -> https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction ; incident ticket -> INC-4231 (private). logging pointer: stackdriver project redwood-prod-eu, logs: `kv.eviction.*`
Carlos (secondary): observed customer abc-corp 502 rate down from 7% -> 3% after first 5 hosts rolled back. still seeing tail latencies for small requests. I'll keep an eye on the SLI dashboard and post updates.
Lena (prod-eng): also adding a cron to rotate hot-shard placement across hosts — low risk, but increases churn if enabled now, so deferring until after stabilization.
Maya (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall: - primary: Maya until 06:30 UTC, then switch to whoever is scheduled in pagerduty. - secondary: Carlos. - active alerts: kv_eviction_rate_high (P2), rpc_5xx_surge (P3 but tied). - mitigations done: rate-limit prefetched traffic, rollback scheduler 5/20 hosts, bumped eviction threshold on eu-canary. - actions pending: finish rollback ring, monitor 10m window for stable evictions, consider disabling prefetch if no improvement after 20 mins. - escalation path: ping Jin -> SRE lead @pager (pager-duty alias) -> oncall manager if >30min no improvement.
Carlos (secondary): adding quick commands for next shift: `curl https://api.redwood.internal/health/kv?region=eu` and `kubectl -n redwood-eu get pods -l app=kv -o wide`. pages for runbook: https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction#metrics
incbot: NOTE: scheduled silence for non-critical noise added for kv_eviction_rate_high in us-west clusters at 2177777660 by Maya.
Maya (oncall): leaving a checklist for whoever picks up at 06:30 UTC — 1) confirm rollback ring completed; 2) check if eviction rate stays <= baseline for 30m; 3) contact affected customers via CS if 502 spike persists; 4) if repeated spike, escalate to infra lead and open postmortem draft.
Jin (sre): I'll stay on standby for 30m then drop out unless escalated. running 'alerts -> group by instance' continually.
Maya (oncall): thanks team. passing handoff to night primary at 06:30 UTC (thread will stay pinned). last note: root cause hypothesis = scheduler prefetch + new health-check timing. record any observed drift in metrics to INC-4231 comments. :thumbsup:
Carlos (secondary): acknowledged, standby.
(END OF THREAD)
